ltl_pairs.nl: Each robot repeatedly fetches an item from the shelf and delivers it to the dock.
A robot must request and hold the dock's exclusive access before entering or occupying the dock to drop off.
A grant remains asserted while its matching request remains asserted.
A robot begins idle at the very first step, with no outstanding dock request yet.
After completing dropoff, a robot releases its dock request IMMEDIATELY -- the very next step.
Every granted lease is eventually released so another waiting robot can be served.
As soon as a robot is carrying an item, it must request the dock without delay.
A robot only heads to the shelf while it is NOT carrying an item.
A robot can pick up only while at the shelf.
A robot can drop off only while at the dock carrying an item.
Action persistence: pickup holds until item is carried.
Grant-gated action persistence: dropoff holds until item is dropped, provided the grant persists.
Each robot does one thing at a time.
ltl_pairs.ltl: G(!(r1_pickup & r1_dropoff) & !(r1_go_to_shelf & r1_go_to_dock) & !(r1_pickup & r1_go_to_dock) & !(r1_pickup & r1_go_to_shelf) & !(r1_dropoff & r1_go_to_shelf) & !(r1_dropoff & r1_go_to_dock))

ltl_pairs.nl: When a robot heads to the shelf it eventually arrives.
When a robot heads to the dock it eventually arrives.
It stays at the shelf until it moves away.
It stays at the dock until it moves away.
A standing request for dock access is eventually granted.
New tasks keep arriving over time.
R1: go_to_shelf is held until at_shelf appears
R1: go_to_dock is held until at_dock appears
R1: world: pickup eventually produces has_item
R1: world: dropoff eventually produces !has_item
R1: world: has_item persists until dropoff
R1: world: !has_item persists until pickup

not_applicable.reason: The system only has one robot instance (Robot1), so mutual exclusion among multiple robots is vacuous.

context: A single robot fetches items from a shelf and requests exclusive arbiter access to deliver them to a shared dock.
